routes.title: Routes

routes.name: Name

routes.archivedBanner: This route is archived: it is excluded from the data plane and its API keys are currently unusable. Restoring resumes the previous state.

providers.title: Providers
providers.empty: No providers yet. Add one first.
providers.name: Label
providers.apiFormatsHint: No format conversion: traffic reaches this provider only when the request format is checked here.
providers.apiFormatsFuture: All three formats have inbound endpoints; the gateway never converts formats, so a request only reaches providers declaring its format.

api.label: API
api.hint: {{name}} is a pay-as-you-go API endpoint using a platform API key.

coding_plan.label: Coding plan
coding_plan.hint: {{name}} is a coding-plan-only endpoint. Subscribe to the plan and use its plan key; a regular pay-as-you-go API key usually will not work.

token_plan.label: Token plan
token_plan.hint: {{name}} is a token-plan-only endpoint. Subscribe to the plan and use its plan key; a regular pay-as-you-go API key usually will not work.

subscription.label: Subscription
subscription.hint: {{name}} is a subscription service. It requires an active subscription or sign-in token, not a regular API key.

local.label: Local
local.hint: {{name}} is a local inference service and needs no platform API key.

enterprise.label: Cloud
enterprise.hint: {{name}} is a cloud-hosted endpoint; you need cloud credentials and model access.

gateway.label: Gateway
gateway.hint: {{name}} is an aggregation/proxy gateway; use the key issued by that gateway.

presetNotes.minimaxAnthropic: MiniMax uses an Anthropic-compatible endpoint. Coding Plan / Token Plan requires the plan key.
presetNotes.anthropicCompatible: This service uses an Anthropic-compatible endpoint; use the platform API key.
presetNotes.kimiCoding: Kimi For Coding exposes both OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints; this entry uses the OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
presetNotes.githubCopilot: Requires an active GitHub Copilot subscription and a short-lived Copilot token; refresh the token when it expires.
presetNotes.opencode: Subscription coding gateway; available models depend on your plan. Use the platform-issued key.
presetNotes.bedrock: Requires AWS credentials (SigV4) and access to Bedrock Claude models.
presetNotes.vertex: Requires a GCP service account and access to Vertex AI Claude models.
presetNotes.poe: Uses a Poe API key; billed by Poe subscription/points, not an official OpenAI key.

providers.statusHint: Disabled providers are excluded from routing
providers.modelsEmpty: No models yet; empty means this provider serves nothing
providers.modelsHint: By default the model ID doubles as the public name; click the pencil to set a separate one (left = upstream model ID, right = name clients see).
providers.fetchNeedsKey: Fill in the API key first
providers.detachedFromPreset: The ID is detached from preset {{preset}}: the Base URL is editable, the variable form is gone, forwarding is unchanged.
providers.fetchNeedsBaseUrl: Fill in the Base URL first
providers.fetchEmpty: Could not fetch models ({{msg}}); enter them manually
providers.autodiscoverFailed: Automatic model discovery failed; you can fetch models later
providers.deleteConfirmDesc: This provider will no longer serve the route. This cannot be undone.
providers.maskedHint: Only the masked value is shown; the plaintext is not retrievable
providers.providerKeyHint: Equals the preset key while bound; copying as custom defaults to <preset>-custom and stays editable.
providers.baseUrlHint: Use the upstream version/compatible prefix (e.g. https://api.deepseek.com or …/v1); the gateway appends /chat/completions or /responses.
providers.priorityHint: Higher wins: within a route every provider in a higher tier is tried before any provider in a lower tier. Only providers in the same tier fall back to the selection strategy. Range 1-1000.
providers.priorityExample: Example: cheap direct account = 2, fallback account = 1 (default 1). To take a provider out of rotation temporarily, switch its status off instead.
providers.serviceAccountPlaceholder: Paste a Google Service Account JSON (client_email / private_key)
providers.serviceAccountHint: Stored encrypted; exchanged for an OAuth2 access token at runtime without reading any environment variables.
providers.vertexPathTemplateHint: Leave empty to derive from publisher + action; supports {project} / {location} / {publisher} / {model} / {action}.
providers.vertexConfigRequired: Vertex requires GCP project and location
providers.lockedHint: Endpoint, formats and auth scheme come from the catalogue preset. Only endpoint variables can be filled; use "Copy as custom" to change anything else.
providers.convertConfirm: Converting detaches this provider from its preset: the Base URL becomes editable and the variable form disappears. Forwarding behaviour is unchanged.
providers.baseUrlPlaceholder: Expanded from the preset, or enter a full URL
providers.credentialPlaceholder: Paste an API key, a Service Account JSON, or AWS credentials JSON (auto-detected)
providers.credentialHint: Three credential forms: API key, Google Service Account JSON, or AWS credentials JSON (access_key_id + secret_access_key); JSON is detected automatically.
providers.credentialServiceAccount: Detected Service Account ({{masked}}): exchanged for an OAuth2 token at runtime.
providers.credentialUnsupported: This credential type does not support model listing or health probing.

tls.title: Built-in HTTPS
tls.hint: Admin only. Once enabled, certificates are issued and renewed automatically for the domains below; no reverse proxy needed.
tls.hstsHint: Off by default; sends Strict-Transport-Security when on
tls.portHint: These are local listen ports; ACME always validates on public port 80 (HTTP-01) or 443 (TLS-ALPN-01). Map ports in front when they differ.
tls.stagingWarning: Staging environment: issued certificates are not trusted by browsers; use it to validate the flow only.
tls.restartRequired: Saved to the database. Listener changes take effect after a restart (renewal does not).
tls.noDomains: No valid domain yet. Add an address like https://gw.example.com under public access URLs.
tls.retryNeedsRestart: Restart the service before issuance can run

selection.title: Selection strategy
selection.hint: Decides which provider is tried first inside this route. It only changes ordering, never request or response bytes.

strategyHints.round_robin: Spreads requests across healthy candidates; identical to the behavior before strategies existed.
strategyHints.uptime: Prefers providers with the lowest failure rate (weights 0.9 / 0.1).
strategyHints.latency: Prefers the lowest time to first byte (weights 0.9 / 0.1).
strategyHints.auto: Scores availability and TTFT together, with a small random exploration.

selection.explorationHint: 0 disables exploration; when exploring, round-robin order is used so new providers gather samples.
selection.fixedWeights: This strategy uses fixed weights (uptime {{uptime}} / TTFT {{latency}}).
selection.fallbackHint: Both weights are 0, so round robin is used.
selection.noProviders: This route has no provider that can take part in selection yet.

incidents.pageHint: All provider incidents. Filter by route, provider, state and time range; closed history is kept.
incidents.title: Open incidents
incidents.hint: Provider failure events. Long-term failures (invalid credentials / exhausted quota) are listed first and can be cleared here.
incidents.bannerManual: {{count}} of them need manual action (invalid credentials / exhausted quota); clear them on the System page

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.hint: Long-term failures are pushed via webhook; transient blips (rate limits / 5xx) are recorded only.
alerts.webhookHint: Leave empty to disable. Only absolute http/https URLs are accepted.
alerts.notifyRecoveryHint: Also push when the incident closes

harness.title: Terminal agent setup
harness.hint: Replace the base URL and key with the ones from the access info above. Each agent speaks a different protocol — see the notes under each tab.

notes.claude-code: Claude Code speaks the Anthropic Messages protocol (POST /v1/messages); a provider in this route must declare Anthropic Messages.
notes.codex: Codex registers a custom provider in ~/.codex/config.toml; pick wire_api according to the formats this route supports (responses or chat).
notes.opencode: OpenCode uses @ai-sdk/openai-compatible against the gateway /v1; the model id is the route client model name.
notes.pi: pi declares a compatible endpoint in ~/.pi/agent/models.json; api is openai-completions (anthropic-messages also works).
notes.generic: Any OpenAI-compatible tool with a configurable base URL can connect this way.

harness.missingFormat: This route does not declare the {{format}} format, so the snippet above is not usable yet; enable that format on a provider first.
harness.keyHint: The key is the gateway API Key from the access info (shown once at creation), not the upstream provider key.
harness.modelHint: Use the client model name declared by providers in this route; each agent examples show where it goes.

desktop.closeToTrayHint: Keep the app running in the tray after the console window is closed; disable to quit on close.
desktop.applyTimeout: The desktop app did not respond, please try again later
desktop.unavailable: This setting is only available in the desktop app (currently running standalone).
